tagline: A week in the open Atlantic around the central group of the Azores: Faial, São Jorge, Terceira and Pico. Volcanic shores, lava terraces above the ocean and Horta marina, its walls painted by crews who have crossed the ocean.

harbor.note: The trip starts and ends at Horta marina on the island of Faial. Departure: 15–22 May 2027.

itinerary.title: A week in the Azores, day by day

summary.title: A loop around the central group of the Azores

itinerary.intro: About 146 miles in a week — the passages are longer than in the Mediterranean; this is the open Atlantic.

days.label: Day 1
days.title: Boarding in Horta
days.text: We meet at the marina on the island of Faial: settling into cabins, meeting the captain and a safety briefing. The quay walls here have been painted by hundreds of crews who have crossed the Atlantic. In the evening, dinner at Peter Café Sport.

days.label: Day 2
days.title: Passage to São Jorge
days.text: We hoist the sails and leave Horta — 22 miles of open water, with dolphins often showing up along the way. By evening we enter Velas, a small port squeezed between the ocean and two-hundred-metre cliffs.

days.label: Day 3
days.title: The fajãs of São Jorge
days.text: A day on the island: we walk down to the fajãs — narrow lava terraces at the foot of the cliffs, beyond the reach of the tourist trails. The finest is Fajã de Santo Cristo, with its lagoon of emerald water. In the evening in Velas we taste a cheese that is made only here.

days.label: Day 4
days.title: Passage to Terceira
days.text: A long leg along the coast — 49 miles. By evening we arrive in Angra do Heroísmo: cobbled streets, a 16th-century cathedral and fortress walls, with the whole centre on the UNESCO World Heritage list.

days.label: Day 5
days.title: A day on Terceira
days.text: A day without sails. We stroll around Angra: old squares, white-stone churches and fish restaurants in the port. For those who like, a descent into the Algar do Carvão volcanic cave with its underground lake.

days.label: Day 6
days.title: Passage to Pico
days.text: The longest passage of the week — 54 miles. Pico is visible long before we get close: the volcanic cone rises straight out of the ocean. We moor in Lajes do Pico, the former whaling capital.

days.label: Day 7
days.title: Pico and the return to Faial
days.text: In the morning — Pico’s vineyards on solidified lava, also a UNESCO site, and the whaling museum. In the afternoon, a short passage back to Horta, 21 miles. In the evening, a farewell dinner on board.

days.label: Day 8
days.title: Disembarkation
days.text: Breakfast on board, packing and disembarkation in the morning. We help with transfers and share the week’s photos.

itinerary.note: The schedule is flexible: the ocean and the forecast may change the order of the days, but not the route itself.
